subject: ED6C3071A4A0E93BF1941116B45ED745
introduction: “Victory” in these prayers means the triumph of a persecuted Faith: that its scattered and endangered believers be protected, its enemies restrained or punished, helpers raised up, and in the end hearts won. The early prayers come from a community “beneath the claws of a pack of wolves”; a run of them in the middle, mostly from the Báb’s writings and Bahá’u’lláh’s early years, ask for vengeance in the language of the imprecatory Psalms; and the guide closes with assurances that a cause that looks weak will prevail slowly, like the dawn. The Psalms, Exodus and the stories of Gideon’s heirs, David and Elisha supply the first kind, “the battle is the Lord’s”, “they that be with us are more than they that be with them”. For the last kind there are Gamaliel’s test, the mustard seed, the leaven and Daniel’s stone. The sharpest company is contrary: Jesus’s “pray for them which despitefully use you”, his rebuke to disciples who wanted fire from heaven, Paul’s “vengeance is mine”, and Mark Twain’s War Prayer on what a prayer for victory leaves unsaid.
questions: What kinds of victory are asked for in this guide? Sort a dozen prayers into protection, punishment, help and the winning of hearts.
The Psalms and readings 39 to 51 pray for enemies to be punished; Jesus says to pray for them. Is there an honest place for both kinds of prayer in a persecuted community’s life?
Twain’s stranger says a prayer for victory is also a prayer for someone’s defeat. Does that apply to a victory of “remembrance and transformed hearts”?
Readings 86 to 94 expect slow triumph. How does that expectation change what one prays for today?
“Not by might, nor by power.” What means of victory do these prayers rule in, and rule out?

outside.why: “These souls are Thy heavenly army.” Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, saith the Lord of hosts.
Paul, of the same kind of army: though we walk in the flesh, we do not war after the flesh: for the weapons of our warfare are not carnal.
“Seize them through Thy power, then aid Thy loved ones.” Let God arise, let his enemies be scattered.
Friends among tyrants. I send you forth as sheep in the midst of wolves.
Adverse winds have encompassed the Lamp of the Covenant. He arose, and rebuked the wind, and said unto the sea, Peace, be still.
Aid Thy servants to assist Thy Cause through wisdom. I will give you a mouth and wisdom, which all your adversaries shall not be able to gainsay.
“When the victory arriveth, every man shall profess himself a believer.” The Qur’an: when Allah’s succour and the triumph cometh and thou seest mankind entering the religion of Allah in troops.
“I beseech Thee by this powerlessness.” My strength is made perfect in weakness.
Transform this weakness into strength and this abasement into glory. He raiseth up the poor out of the dust, to set them among princes.
That which shall transform sorrow into joy. Your sorrow shall be turned into joy.
Thy loved ones encompassed by the rebellious. Fear not: for they that be with us are more than they that be with them.
The oppressors have wronged Thy loved ones. How long, O Lord, holy and true, dost thou not judge?
Sincere servants scattered throughout the regions. He that scattered Israel will gather him.
The wolves have seized Thy sheep. I am the good shepherd: the good shepherd giveth his life for the sheep.
Put forth the hand of Thine omnipotence. Stand still, and see the salvation of the Lord.
It behoves every believer to hold fast and be patient. Wait on the Lord: be of good courage.
By the light whereby Thou didst deliver Noah. But Noah found grace in the eyes of the Lord.
“Send down unto me victory from Thy presence.” Some trust in chariots, and some in horses: but we will remember the name of the Lord our God.
By the blood shed in Thy path. The voice of thy brother’s blood crieth unto me from the ground.
As a captive beseeches the King. Out of the depths have I cried unto thee, O Lord.

“Render Thy Cause victorious, O my Lord, and abase Thou Thine enemies.” Mark Twain imagined a stranger explaining to a congregation what a prayer for victory also asks: when you have prayed for victory you have prayed for many unmentioned results which follow victory. He was writing of a war of armies. What is the “victory” in these prayers, and who loses by it?
Make them triumphant and steadfast. In all these things we are more than conquerors through him that loved us.
Withhold from us the harm of the wicked. God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble.
“Chastise those who denied Thy most great signs.” The Psalter has such prayers: break their teeth, O God, in their mouth.
“Cut off the hands that were stretched forth against them.” Do not I hate them, O Lord, that hate thee? I hate them with perfect hatred.

Readings 39 to 51 are prayers of the Báb and Bahá’u’lláh for the punishment of persecutors, in the manner of the Psalms. Jesus taught another prayer: love your enemies, bless them that curse you, pray for them which despitefully use you. Both kinds are in this guide (see 86 onward, and the companion guide on justice). How do you hold them together?

“Purify the earth from Thy enemies.” Disciples who wished to call down fire on a village were told: ye know not what manner of spirit ye are of. For the Son of man is not come to destroy men’s lives, but to save them.

“Seize Thine enemies.” Paul allows the wish and forbids the deed: avenge not yourselves, but rather give place unto wrath: vengeance is mine; I will repay, saith the Lord. What is the moral difference between asking God to punish and doing it?
“Hasten Thy vengeance.” O Lord, how long shall I cry, and thou wilt not hear!
Hosts arrayed from the Kingdom. We wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against the rulers of the darkness of this world.
That the army of light may be victorious. The light shineth in darkness; and the darkness comprehended it not.
Through the hosts of the Supreme Concourse. Seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses.
“Aid Thou Thy loved ones, and them that aid them.” If Allah is your helper none can overcome you.
Aid me and those with me. Be not afraid nor dismayed by reason of this great multitude; for the battle is not yours, but God’s.
Succour them through Thy power. The Lord saveth not with sword and spear: for the battle is the Lord’s.
Send down the hosts of heaven. They fought from heaven; the stars in their courses fought against Sisera.
Raise up servants who will aid Thy Cause. The harvest truly is plenteous, but the labourers are few; pray ye therefore the Lord of the harvest.
“Make us helpers of Thy religion.” O ye who believe! Be Allah’s helpers, even as Jesus son of Mary said unto the disciples: who are my helpers for Allah?
“I have desired naught but the exaltation of Thy Cause.” He must increase, but I must decrease.
The station of the apostles was not known in their time. Gamaliel: if this work be of men, it will come to nought: but if it be of God, ye cannot overthrow it.
Will the spiritual ultimately prevail? In the world ye shall have tribulation: but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world.
This is but the beginning of the dawn. The path of the just is as the shining light, that shineth more and more unto the perfect day.
The foundations laid; what is latent will appear. The least of all seeds becometh a tree.
In ages to come the Cause will grow a hundredfold. The stone that smote the image became a great mountain, and filled the whole earth.
A flame that warms more than a little space. The kingdom is like leaven, till the whole was leavened.
We will succeed; but could our own failures delay it? Let him that thinketh he standeth take heed lest he fall. What part do the believers’ own shortcomings play in the victory prayed for?
Whatever may befall this infant Faith. Upon this rock I will build my church; and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it.
John’s definition of the word the whole guide turns on: this is the victory that overcometh the world, even our faith.

shortfall: Readings 24 to 35 and 59 to 85 are petitions for aid and victory by one Name after another, nearly alike, and they share the companions given; the count is about half the guide’s for that reason.

psalm-let-god-arise.text: Let God arise, let his enemies be scattered: let them also that hate him flee before him. As smoke is driven away, so drive them away: as wax melteth before the fire, so let the wicked perish at the presence of God

psalm-break-their-teeth.text: Break their teeth, O God, in their mouth: break out the great teeth of the young lions, O Lord

romans-more-than-conquerors.text: Nay, in all these things we are more than conquerors through him that loved us
